Measured against the stronger model alone, across 48 pairs of 12 open-weight models (3B to 72B) in math, knowledge, code and reasoning, review beats it in only 9 of 96 review directions, and does worse the larger the capability gap. The reason is anchoring: the reviewer mostly follows the generator, discarding its own correct answers. Review costs 2.6 to 2.8 times as much as the stronger model alone, while a selector using the same two calls is 2.7 to 4.2 points more accurate than review and cheaper. Studies of verification should report the stronger model alone, not only the gain over the generator.

paper_title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
paper_abstract: Large Language Models accelerate software development but introduce severe security vulnerabilities. This systematic review investigates security risks in automated coding, benchmark limitations, and the role of human developers. Findings indicate that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases. Additionally, the models themselves are susceptible to direct attacks. Current evaluation methods suffer from data contamination and lack robust security metrics. Consequently, human oversight remains essential. Safer integration of automation will require more security-aware model architectures, stronger security-specific benchmarks, and more effective human-AI collaboration frameworks to mitigate these systemic risks.
comments: 35 pages Accepted for publication in ACM Computing Surveys (CSUR). A copy of the formal acceptance letter can be verified via the publisher's portal or provided to moderators upon request

paper_title: From Acoustic Sensing to Physical Actions: A Comprehensive Survey of Security Risks in Edge-Deployed Audio LLM-Based Agents
paper_abstract: Audio Large Language Models (Audio LLMs) are embedded in agents for smart homes, vehicles, wearables, and embodied systems, where acoustic inputs can propagate from perception into persistent state and consequential execution. This setting extends security analysis beyond model behavior to the system conditions that determine how acoustic inputs can influence agent behavior and external actions. Existing surveys examine acoustic security, LLM-based agents, and edge deployment in isolation, leaving their security interactions in deployed Audio LLM-based agents insufficiently characterized. This survey introduces an Acoustic Sensing-to-Action (S2A) system model that traces these security implications along the path from acoustic sensing to external execution, while accounting for edge-cloud runtime and lifecycle transformation. We use the model to synthesize attacks, defenses, and evaluation methods across the acoustic, agent, and edge-system literature. The synthesis shows that security gaps can emerge within components and at the transitions between stages, where protections developed for one stage do not necessarily provide end-to-end assurance in the deployed system. These findings motivate security evaluation that follows acoustic influence from sensing to action across persistent state, system boundaries, and changing deployment conditions in real-world agents.

paper_title: From Trajectories to Experience: A Survey of Experience-Driven LLM Agents
paper_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can plan, use tools, and recover from errors within a task, yet many carry little from one task to the next and repeat mistakes they have already resolved. The root cause is a lack of experience accumulation: trajectories record what failed and how the agent recovered, but this information is seldom turned into guidance for later tasks. Research on this capability spans reflection, agent memory, workflow learning, and skill acquisition, but these lines describe similar content in different terms and lack a common account of experience itself, leaving basic questions open: what counts as experience, how it should be accumulated, used, and revised, and how to tell whether it improves later behavior. This survey addresses these questions with a unified framework. We define agent experience as action-guiding information grounded in task trajectories and retained to guide later episodes where it applies, whether as a trajectory precedent, a semantic lesson, or a reusable procedure. We focus on explicitly accessible experience, including its use as a training signal for internalization into model parameters. We describe each unit of experience by its guidance, applicability conditions, execution evidence, and reliability evaluation, so that memory entries, workflows, and skills become directly comparable, and follow experience through four lifecycle functions---formation, organization, utilization, and maintenance---that determine how it is accumulated, used, and revised. To judge reported gains, we distinguish three improvement claims---fixed experience reuse, feedback-driven sustained improvement, and improvement of the learning mechanism---by the evidence each requires. Current studies most clearly support fixed experience reuse, chiefly on tasks with tests or reference answers; evidence for the other two claims remains partial. Our analysis yields recommendations for seven application settings and a central design principle: keep guidance connected to its applicability conditions and to the evidence that supports or challenges it. Finally, we outline eight open problems, from learning with human expert records to testing whether gains accumulate, toward agents whose improvement is cumulative, transferable, and correctable.

paper_title: <span data-teams="true">Digital Transformation and the Adoption of Strategic Management Accounting Among Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Soweto, South Africa: A Literature Review
paper_abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed the operational and strategic landscape of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs), creating opportunities to improve organisational performance through digitally enabled Strategic Management Accounting (SMA). While traditional management accounting primarily supports operational control and historical financial reporting, SMA extends this role by integrating financial and non-financial information to facilitate strategic planning, competitive positioning, and long-term decision-making. The emergence of cloud computing, artificial intelligence, enterprise resource planning systems, big data analytics, blockchain, and mobile accounting has significantly enhanced the ability of SMEs to generate timely, accurate, and strategic information. Despite these opportunities, the adoption of digitally enabled SMA remains uneven, particularly among township-based SMEs operating in resource-constrained environments such as Soweto, South Africa. Existing literature indicates that organisational limitations, technological barriers, infrastructural deficiencies, regulatory uncertainty, and inadequate managerial capabilities continue to constrain digital transformation within SMEs. Furthermore, much of the existing research has focused on large organisations and developed economies, resulting in limited understanding of how digital transformation influences SMA adoption within township businesses. This literature review critically synthesises current scholarly evidence regarding Strategic Management Accounting, digital transformation, theoretical explanations for technology adoption, and the organisational factors influencing digitally enabled SMA implementation among SMEs. The review further identifies major research gaps and proposes future research directions that contribute to both theory and practice by providing a context-specific understanding of digital transformation and strategic accounting within South African township economies.

paper_title: Designing Artificial Intelligence Decision Support for Periodontal Care in Kazakhstan: A Three-Stakeholder Cross-Sectional Survey of Dentists, Primary Care Physicians and Patients
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools for periodontal diagnosis are proliferating, yet little is known about what clinicians and patients in Central Asia expect from such systems. We elicited requirements for an AI-enabled periodontal decision-support system from three stakeholder groups in Kazakhstan and examined which patient-reported risk factors are associated with self-reported signs of periodontal disease. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey (July–September 2026) enrolled 33 dentists, 91 primary health care (PHC) physicians and medical specialists, and 455 patients with periodontal disease. Proportions were reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CI); groups were compared with Fisher’s exact, χ², Mann–Whitney and Kruskal–Wallis tests with effect sizes; multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with self-reported periodontal signs. Results: Dentists prioritised automation of history-taking (81.8%) and visual gingival assessment (72.7%), and named early gingivitis diagnosis as the stage where AI is most needed (69.7%). Only human-controlled autonomy levels were chosen; the most frequently cited barrier was the absence of a legal framework and liability insurance (60.6%), and dentists with >5 years of experience more often demanded mandatory verification or a prohibition of full autonomy (exact p = 0.045; Cramér’s V = 0.54). PHC physicians considered early gingivitis screening their most effective contribution (80.2%) but cited insufficient competence as the main barrier (53.8%). Self-reported periodontal signs were present in 49.0% of patients and were independently associated with high stress (adjusted odds ratio 2.11; 95% CI 1.14–3.89) and a positive family history (1.61; 1.02–2.55); six symptom items did not form a reliable scale (Cronbach’s α = 0.56). Conclusions: Stakeholders in Kazakhstan favour a low-autonomy, clinician-verified AI system focused on early gingivitis detection, interprofessional data sharing and clearly regulated accountability. These requirements provide an evidence base for the design and governance of periodontal AI in emerging health systems.

paper_title: Keeping the Core, Adapting the Periphery: Structured Comparative Review of the Transfer of a Group Singing Intervention for Postnatal Depression from the United Kingdom to Denmark, Romania, and Italy
paper_abstract: Background: A ten-week group singing programme for mothers with symptoms of postnatal depression (PND) has been evaluated in two randomised controlled trials in the United Kingdom. Under the coordination of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Europe, it was subsequently implemented in Denmark, Romania, and Italy. It is unclear which components of the programme transferred unchanged, which were adapted, and how strong the underlying evidence is. Methods: We conducted a structured comparative review of four primary studies: two British trials and two implementation studies. The intervention in each setting was described using the TIDieR checklist. Adaptations were coded using the FRAME framework, and outcomes were mapped to the RE-AIM dimensions. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2 (randomised trials) and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (other designs). Certainty of evidence was judged using GRADE principles. Where possible, we calculated standardised effect sizes and absolute differences in retention. Results: In the larger trial (N = 199), mothers in the singing group had lower Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scores than an active community control group at week 20 (treatment effect −1.59; approximately 0.41 baseline standard deviations) and week 36 (−1.56; approximately 0.40). The effect was not significant in an available-data analysis, and the trial was judged at high risk of bias because of differential attrition. Retention was 28 percentage points higher in the singing group at week 36 (66% vs. 38%). In Italy, 23 mothers attended a mean of 87% of sessions and none dropped out. Across settings, four components were retained everywhere: the ten-week group format, a trained singing leader, the presence of infants, and a non-medical framing. Recruitment, venue, session length, staffing, and repertoire were modified. Thirteen modifications were coded, of which nine were planned and three unplanned. Attitudes to mental illness and trust in health services shaped implementation more than language did. Conclusions: The programme's core transferred intact, and its acceptability was consistently high. Certainty that it reduces depressive symptoms is low, and there is no controlled evidence of effectiveness outside the United Kingdom.

paper_title: UAV Communication Security: A Narrative Review of Lightweight Authentication, ECC, and Hardware-Software Trade-Offs
paper_abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles increasingly exchange commands, telemetry, and mission data through interconnected ground, edge, and aerial networks. Their communication security depends on authentication, key management, implementation assurance, and constrained resources rather than on a cryptographic primitive alone. This narrative review examines lightweight authentication for UAV networks, with emphasis on the role of elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) and the trade-offs among software, FPGA, and hybrid implementations. Representative protocol studies are organized by communicating parties, trust assumptions, supporting mechanisms, and reported evidence. Standards for authenticated key establishment, authenticated encryption, and post-quantum cryptography provide a separate reference layer. The synthesis distinguishes mathematical security claims, symbolic protocol analysis, software timing, hardware realization, and operational deployment. ECC can support compact classical public-key mechanisms, but it does not independently provide message confidentiality, replay protection, capture resistance, or quantum resistance. PUF-assisted and infrastructure-assisted designs redistribute trust and implementation costs rather than eliminating them. A reporting framework identifies the information needed for meaningful comparisons, including credential provisioning, state recovery, communication overhead, and end-to-end energy. The review presents no new authentication protocol or experimental benchmark; its contribution is a critical, implementation-aware organization of the evidence and research gaps.

paper_title: Grid-Forming Electric Vehicles: A Critical Review of Bidirectional Charging, AI-Enabled Control, and Grid-Support Services
paper_abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are evolving from passive charging loads into grid-supporting resources. Conventional smart-charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) strategies treat the charger as a grid-following current source that depends on a stiff external voltage, a dependence that becomes a weakness as inverter-based resources displace synchronous inertia. Grid-forming (GFM) control instead operates the bidirectional charger as a voltage source that establishes local voltage and frequency, enabling weak-grid, islanded, and black-start operation. This review synthesizes 113 sources, most identified through a structured keyword-based search, and organizes them along an evolutionary framework running from conventional charging through V2G and GFM EVs to AI-adaptive, fleet-coordinated resources. It covers bidirectional converter topologies; droop, virtual synchronous machine, virtual oscillator, and matching control; AI-enabled control using neural, fuzzy, reinforcement-learning, predictive, and physics-informed methods; fleet aggregation; resilience and black start; battery constraints; and cybersecurity and standardization. Throughout, experimentally demonstrated capability is distinguished from simulation-only or theoretical results. The synthesis shows that documented field pilots still rely on grid-following control and that GFM-EV validation remains largely confined to simulation. Seven research gaps are identified, including experimental validation, AI verifiability, battery–grid objective conflict, and fleet-scale coordination, and a five-generation roadmap toward autonomous, resilient GFM-EV fleets is proposed.

paper_title: Taxonomic Survey of Culture-Enriched Metagenomes from Gram-Negative Bacteria in Pigs, Piggery Environments, and Humans Associated with Pig Production Systems in Okada, Edo State, Nigeria
paper_abstract: Pig farming significantly supports livestock agriculture, food security, livelihoods, household income, and employment across developing countries, including Nigeria. This study characterized Gram-negative bacteria from pig production systems at Okada, Edo State, Nigeria, using a One Health approach of integrating animal, environmental and human-associated compartments. A total of 356 samples were collected and examined from the three compartments comprising, 132 pig-associated (37.08%), 124 environmental (34.83%), and 100 human-associated (28.09%). Cultural and biochemical examinations yielded 48 Gram-negative isolates, consisting of 22 isolates (45.83%) from pigs, 14 isolates (29.17%) from environmental sources, and 12 isolates (25.00%) from humans. The isolates comprised Proteus, Enterobacter, Pseudomonas, Escherichia, Klebsiella, Bordetella, Morganella, Providencia and Citrobacter, with Proteus predominating (13; 27.08%). Although bacterial genera varied numerically among compartments, Pearson’s chi-square test showed no significant association between bacterial genus and compartment (χ² = 11.25, p = 0.79). Whole-genome shotgun sequencing generated high-quality data, with mean reads exceeding 17 million and Q30 scores, with 95.50–96.50% of reads retained after filtering. Krona analysis showed predominance of Proteobacteria, Gammaproteobacteria and Enterobacterales across the compartments. Proteus spp (> 20%) and Bordetella trematum(16%), were prominent among pig-associated sequences; Proteus spp (>22%) and Escherichia coli(14%), predominated among human-associated sequences; environmental profiles were more heterogeneous, with E. coli, Citrobacter freundii, Klebsiella variicola each contributing approximately 9%. Seventeen species and a genus Halomonas were identified, with nine species shared across the three compartments. Cochran’s Q test showed no significant difference in species representation (Q = 1.14, p = 0.57). Jaccard similarity was highest between environmental and human-associated compartments (0.733), indicating substantial taxonomic connectivity. Overall, the findings support integrated One Health surveillance of Gram-negative bacteria in pig production.

paper_title: Polysaccharide-Based Edible Coating As a Sustainable Preservation Technique for Post -Harvest Shelf-Life Extension of Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum): A Review
paper_abstract: The persistence Postharvest losses of Tomato and other perishable fruits rise an urgenet need biodegradable and environmentally benign preservation methods. Polysaccharide-based edible coatings have shown great potential as alternatives to conventional synthetic methods for postharvest treatments due to their film-forming ability, biodegradability, biocompatibility, antimicrobial, and antioxidant carrier capabilities. This review examines the application of polysaccharide edible coatings as a sustainable preservation technique for tomatoes and other selected perishable fruits by considering their sources, functional and structural properties, in edible coating applications, focusing on their concentrations and preservation outcomes. Findings from published studies reveal that polysaccharide-based coatings reduce physiological weight loss, respiration rate, softening, ethylene production, colour change, and microbial damage, while enhancing nutritional constituents, hence extending the overall postharvest shelf life. Depending on the polymer concentration, molecular properties, fruit species, storage temperature, and coating formulation, it further demonstrated that, incorporating coatings with two or more polysaccharides, essential oils, plant extracts, and nanoparticles show improved preservative properties. The study suggests further studies on the development of low-cost, multifunctional, food-safe, polysaccharide-based coatings, especially those sourced from agricultural waste and other locally available resources. Such innovations could significantly contribute to sustainable postharvest control, food security, and environmentally benign food packaging systems.

paper_title: Malware Detection with Autonomous Agents: A Review of Functional Roles, Datasets, and Coordination Readiness
paper_abstract: Large language models are increasingly written into malware detection systems, yet the literature reports them under a single label that obscures what they actually do, and existing surveys either treat agents in the abstract or malware detection without them. This review closes that gap. It is the first to examine the implemented strand of agent-based malware detection as a coordinated system rather than a catalogue of techniques, and to ask how well positioned the field is to support multi-agent operation. We make three contributions. First, we introduce a functional classification that groups each system by which of four roles the model fills, namely perception, reasoning and decision-making, adaptive monitoring, and collaborative learning, treating the mature body of standalone detectors as the foundation rather than the object of review. Second, from a corpus of recent primary studies we derive a modality-based dataset taxonomy, a map linking datasets to the role the model plays, and a pipeline-stage and role-coverage matrix for the agent-based systems. Third, we assess which existing detectors are structurally ready for agentisation and why. The analysis yields three findings. What varies across the field is not which model is used but where in the detection chain it sits. Role coverage is bimodal, with perception and reasoning served almost everywhere while adaptive monitoring is realised by a single system in the corpus and collaborative learning by none. And uniformly high reported accuracy reflects curated, single-split evaluation rather than robustness. Reading these together, the discriminating property for agentisation is whether a system exposes anything between input and verdict, which makes integration and orchestration, not the invention of new detectors, the principal open problem.

paper_title: From Detection to Investigation: A Survey of Foundation Models and Agents for Financial Fraud and Financial Crime
paper_abstract: Foundation models are extending research on financial fraud and financial crime from isolated risk detection to document understanding, relational analysis, and investigative workflows. A gap nevertheless separates model outputs from candidate evidence and actionable conclusions. This survey examines advances in six families of foundation models: language, vision, speech, temporal, graph, and tabular models. It compares their roles and limitations along two dimensions: the risk-control lifecycle and the directness of the supporting evidence. Existing studies show that pretraining can support representation reuse and the processing of unstructured information, with direct validation in some financial tasks. Cross-modal identity binding, information availability over time, report faithfulness, and case-level benefits require separate evaluation. Evidence on investigative agents spans prototypes, controlled tasks, expert assessments, and industry disclosures, which establish different aspects of workflow feasibility, task performance, and user assessment. Establishing gains in investigative efficiency and reductions in financial losses requires case-level comparative evidence. We examine entity and temporal alignment, the organization of candidate evidence, constrained tool execution, and investigative benchmark design, together with the implications of adversarial threats, privacy, fairness, and model risk governance. Research priorities should shift from expanding system functionality toward factual traceability, sufficient evidence for decisions, and reviewable actions.

paper_title: From 3D Scene Understanding to Hazard Forecasting: A Critical Review of Remote Sensing–Driven Emergency Digital Twins
paper_abstract: Emergency forecasts benefit from scene detail when it constrains the relevant physical process and reaches decision-makers in time. This critical review examines flood inundation, wildfire spread and marine drift through 148 sources and 16 purpose-selected study families. Within this selected corpus, four families develop dedicated 3D conversion, chiefly for hydraulic-domain or fuel-material preparation; the coding rule excludes routine terrain input and existing ocean analyses. Forecast cases mainly update states, controls or initial trajectories. Hydraulic connectivity can alter local inundation. Corrected fire fronts remain exposed to propagation error, while wider marine search regions improve coverage at increased search cost. These mechanisms explain why geometric accuracy and analysis fit alone cannot establish predictive value. We propose a framework that selects scene attributes, update targets and observation timing jointly. Matched alternatives share a future response quantity, information cutoff and resource budget; deployment-specific tolerances connect their comparison to evacuation requirements and search capacity. Physically coupled neural representations require calibrated material properties and an online delivery-time account. The proposed tests assess the forecast effect of additional scene detail, the persistence of a correction and the time left for response.

paper_title: Impacts and Adaptations to Extreme Weather Events on Pathology Laboratories: A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Pathology laboratories are a critical dependency across almost every diagnostic and treatment pathway. Pathology laboratories support healthcare delivery through analysing blood, urine, faecal and tissue samples, informing clinical diagnosis and tailoring patient treatment. However, laboratories have unique vulnerabilities to extreme weather events. To analyse samples and provide timely results, laboratories need highly-controlled environments and timelines. EWE can disrupt these and, when pathology laboratories fail or slow down during EWE, many healthcare services are disrupted simultaneously. In this study we have reviewed the impacts of heatwaves and flooding on pathology laboratories in G20 and European Union countries and any adaptation strategies that laboratories have put in place to mitigate those impacts. The PRISMA guidance was followed for a systematic search strategy that identified 1,133 articles for screening. Seven of these were included after full-text screening. Together with an additional two articles from backward citation searches, a total of nine articles were included in this review. Three reviewers were involved in this process. We found reports of widespread impacts of heatwaves and flooding on pathology laboratory staff, equipment, operations and internal and external supply chains. The perspectives of patients were mostly absent. While there were examples of adaptations deployed, we found little evidence of systematic evaluation to determine the cost-benefit of these adaptations, their health consequences or their impacts on health inequalities. Climate change will lead to more intense, frequent, volatile and unpredictable extreme weather events in most countries, which will increase pathology laboratory disruptions and subsequent impacts on healthcare pathways and patients. This should be a call for further action and the development of frameworks to enable pathology laboratories to implement and evaluate adaptations to extreme weather events-related disruptions that minimise disruption and deliver resilient pathology service provision to support patient care.

paper_title: Clinical Photography in UK Podiatric Practice A Narrative Review of Consent, Confidentiality and Safe Image Handling
paper_abstract: A clinical photograph can show changes that are difficult to describe in words. In podiatry, images help document wounds and skin lesions, support referrals and compare progress over time. They also create a lasting record that may identify the patient, even when the face is absent. This narrative review brings together UK legislation, professional guidance and selected literature to explain how photographs should be taken, stored and used. The starting point is the intended purpose. Agreement to a photograph for care does not automatically permit teaching, research, publication or promotion, and the patient’s agreement is distinct from the organisation’s data-protection basis for processing the image. The proposed framework covers the patient discussion, image capture, record linkage, storage, secondary use and audit. Its practical message is simple: a clinical photograph needs the same care as the rest of the patient’s health record.

paper_title: MCDM Applications for Sustainability Assessment in Textile and Apparel Supply Chains: A Systematic Review of Methods, Contexts, and Criteria
paper_abstract: Sustainability in the textile supply chain involves complex trade-offs across economic, environmental and social aspects, driven by the variability in materials, manufacturing processes and technologies, industrial management, geographical locations, working conditions, logistics, and product use. While multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods have been increasingly applied to navigate these trade-offs, existing reviews have narrowly focused on bibliometric trends, offering limited insight into the contextual application and sustainability criteria used in these assessments. This study addresses this gap through a systematic literature review by analysing 96 studies that investigate the application of MCDM methods in sustainability management across the textile supply chain, with specific attention to methodological rigor and contextual relevance. The review identifies two key research dimensions: (1) the MCDM methods employed and their application contexts in respective scope of studies, and (2) the applied and prioritized criteria for sustainability management in textile industries. Results show that the identification of influential factors for sustainability implementation is the most common scope of study, with DEMATEL being the dominant MCDM tool and identifying government policies as the most influential factor. This is followed by sustainable supplier selection, with frequent use of hybrid AHP-TOPSIS methods, often in fuzzy settings, and a predominant focus on economic criteria, particularly cost and financial flexibility. The majority of corporate sustainability assessments rely on quantitative environmental data derived from corporate reports, and public data and use single-method MCDM models without explicit weighting schemes. Product-level assessments commonly employ distance-based MCDM methods to support the interpretation of Life Cycle Assessment results or to expand the sustainability perspective by incorporating economic and social dimensions. This review advances the understanding of how MCDM methods support sustainability decision-making in different contexts and settings of textile supply chain and highlights key criteria shaping such evaluations.

paper_title: Continuous Risk-Based Scheduling for Food Safety Inspection: Integrating Historical Decay with Event-Driven Consumer Review Signals
paper_abstract: Batch risk-based inspection scheduling struggles to detect a critical failure class: food facilities with recent clean inspections that subsequently develop severe violations. Traditional systems recompute risk on fixed planning cycles using static historical data, leaving blind spots between inspection cycles. To address this, we introduce the Continuous Inspection Risk (CIR) system, an event-driven scheduling pipeline that re-ranks the inspection queue dynamically as new data arrives. CIR combines a decay-weighted historical score with a stream of real-time consumer reviews triaged by a language-model classifier. A key structural contribution is our temporal partition rule, which strictly excludes reviews predating the most recent inspection to prevent superseded signals from skewing current risk. Evaluating CIR on 9,505 routine inspections in Santa Clara County, California (2024-2026), we show that history-based scoring alone reduces mean time-to-detection of major violations by 69 days (20.9%) under a 30% inspection budget, but fails to anticipate severe vermin-related closures (0/8 detected). Incorporating post-inspection review signals drastically improves performance, predicting 7 of 8 vermin closures with an average lead time of 117 days-firing on the exact day of review publication in four instances. Introducing a review corroboration rule improves precision from 0.70 to 0.78 without loss of recall. Finally, we analyze critical implementation challenges, documenting a data-hygiene pitfall (stale review leakage across inspection boundaries) and an evaluation limitation involving unobserved facility self-remediation. This work provides the first case-level evaluation of event-driven inspection triggering using open data and provides a reproducible benchmark for review-augmented public health systems

paper_title: Probable but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of Decision Models as Synthetic Survey Respondents
paper_abstract: Language models are increasingly used to create synthetic survey samples, also called silicon samples. Decision models are a new class of language models that return a probability for each point of a rating scale instead of text. We ask whether these models, or the newest generative LLMs, can stand in for human respondents on a psychometric survey. We test fourteen decision models from eleven providers and 47 generative LLMs on an open Lithuanian organisational-psychology survey (n=263, 68 items), with 100 real respondent profiles, the Psychometric Similarity Score (PSS) and statistical baselines. The best generative model, MiniMax M3, reaches PSS 0.813. This is level with a Gaussian copula fit only on other respondents (0.824) and below a copula fit in sample (0.927). A second sample of 100 real people scores below the best models, so at this size PSS cannot rank them against real respondents. In 5 of 10 product lines the newest generative release scores below an earlier release of the same line beyond resampling noise, and none gains beyond it. With the default rounded readout, 13 of 14 decision models score below the generative reference gpt-5.4-mini. Of the 47 generative models, 33 reproduce the pattern of item correlations better than any decision model. Averaged over respondents, the probability vectors are much closer to the human item marginals than rounded answers. They also rank respondents about as well as a profile regression fit on 163 real people. As forecasts of each person's own answers, however, every decision model is worse than the answer frequencies of other respondents, mainly because its average vector differs from them. The profile regression improves on these frequencies by only 1.0%, so the profile fields say little about how a person answers. Synthetic respondents built on such profiles should therefore aim at sample-level fidelity.

paper_title: Signal-Amplification Strategies for Gold-Nanoparticle Lateral Flow Assays: A Structured Review of Limit-of-Detection Improvement Relative to Conventional GNP-LFA
paper_abstract: Gold-nanoparticle lateral flow assays (GNP-LFAs) are attractive for point-of-care testing, but their conventional colorimetric readout often limits analytical sensitivity. This structured review asked which signal-amplification strategies produce the greatest improvement in limit of detection (LOD) relative to a conventional GNP-LFA comparator, and by what magnitude. Candidate records were identified through an investigator-directed keyword search and screened at full text by a single reviewer; 29 of 36 assessed records met eligibility, contributing 36 comparator arms across nine mechanism categories. Reported LOD fold-improvements ranged from no measurable gain to 1000x. Enzyme/catalytic (nanozyme) amplification spanned the widest range (4x–1000x across 5 arms), whereas silver/gold enhancement was the most frequently reported category (7 arms, 4 studies), with gains mostly below 40x and one study reporting up to 488x. Two arms showed no meaningful improvement over a conventional or visual-readout comparator. Gains varied substantially within and between categories and were analyte- and format-dependent; same-study and literature-baseline comparators answer different questions and should not be treated interchangeably. The largest gains came from mechanisms acting on detection chemistry rather than flow control or label loading, although most categories rest on few independent studies. Single-reviewer screening and an investigator-directed search are limitations.

paper_title: Integrated Development of Spatial Regeneration and the Cultural and Creative Industries in Chinese Traditional Villages: A Correlational Literature Review
paper_abstract: Spatial regeneration and the cultural and creative industries (CCIs) are paired in policies for China’s traditional villages, yet seldom examined together. This correlational literature review analyzes the full texts of 35 peer-reviewed case studies published in 2017–2026. The corpus was assembled purposively; a later check of two bibliographic databases flagged at least 238 further potentially eligible records, so the 35 papers cover only part of the literature. Each paper was coded for regeneration strategies, CCI categories, village type, governance mode, outcomes, and conflicts, and the analysis combines keyword co-occurrence, φ coefficients, and a qualitative classification of outcomes. Five of six regeneration strategies are reported in more than two-thirds of the papers. Cultural tourism is reported in every paper, followed by performing arts, crafts, and museums, whereas architecture, design, film, and digital content appear in eight papers. No strategy–category association remains significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Of 140 outcome judgments, 47.1% are realized positive, 35.7% mixed, and 10.0% realized negative; negative results concentrate in the social dimension. The sample is too small to test differences by region, village type, or governance mode. In these papers, the link between spatial regeneration and cultural activity is documented almost exclusively through tourism.

paper_title: From Prediction to Decision: A Critical Review of AI Agents for Cancer Treatment and the Evaluation Gap
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence for cancer treatment is undergoing a transition from predicting outcomes to supporting decisions. Early systems estimated the probability of response or survival; emerging agents built on large language models (LLMs) retrieve evidence, invoke tools, and deliberate over guidelines to produce treatment recommendations. We argue that this shift changes not only what these systems do but what they are: a recommender, unlike a probabilistic estimator, cannot be validated by discrimination metrics alone. We trace this trajectory across four generations of systems; analyze pathology foundation models as the perceptual substrate of agents and the information bottleneck separating perception from reasoning; dissect four agent architectures and the failure modes each introduces; and show, through a running biliary-tract-cancer stress test, three qualitative gaps—quantitative pharmacological reasoning, molecular resistance reasoning, and inter-guideline conflict resolution—that no current system addresses. Our central finding is an evaluation gap: agents function as clinical decision support systems yet are validated on task accuracy or expert concordance—the latter a metric rendered circular by documented inter-board variability—while no system has reported patient-level outcome evidence. We formalize patient-conditional evidence conflict and propose design principles, a three-tier evaluation framework, and a phased translation protocol toward clinically credible agents.

paper_title: Structural and Psychosocial Drivers of ART Refill Non-Attendance in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Literature Review
paper_abstract: Background: Missed antiretroviral therapy (ART) refills are an early warning sign of treatment interruption and loss to follow-up among people living with HIV in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). This review synthesized evidence on the structural and psychosocial drivers of ART refill non-attendance among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in SSA. Methods: We searched PubMed, PubMed Central, and Google Scholar and grey literature for studies (2000–2026) on barriers to ART refills or clinic attendance in SSA, and synthesized findings thematically as structural or psychosocial drivers. Results: Structural drivers included long clinic waits, staffing, and medication availability, transport costs, distance, and policy or financing disruptions. Psychosocial drivers included stigma, depression, limited social support, low health literacy, and poor patient-provider relationships. The domains interact; crowded clinics, for example, heighten stigma. Evidence is limited by inconsistent definitions, cross-sectional designs, and geographic concentration. Conclusions: Refill non-attendance reflects interconnected structural and psychosocial factors. Multi-level responses, combining decentralized differentiated service delivery with mental health support and stigma reduction, are needed, alongside standardized definitions and research on underexplored populations.

paper_title: Threat Appraisal Coping Appraisal and Secure Networking Intention among Technology Users in Bangladesh: An Exploratory Survey Analysis
paper_abstract: Protection motivation theory distinguishes perceived threat from evaluations of protective responses, but interpreting their relationships requires dependable measures. This exploratory cross-sectional study assessed measurement quality and appraisal-related associations with secure networking practice intention in 385 complete questionnaire records from Bangladesh. Threat appraisal, coping appraisal and intention were represented by their respective three-item means. Internal consistency, heterotrait–monotrait ratios and a bounded covariance diagnostic were examined before hierarchical regression with HC3 standard errors, 2,000 bootstrap resamples and ten-fold cross-validation. Threat appraisal was positively associated with intention (b = 0.233, 95% CI 0.138–0.328), as was coping appraisal (b = 0.347, 95% CI 0.254–0.440). The interaction was unsupported (b = 0.002, p = .981), and the additive model performed slightly better in held-out prediction. Measurement evidence was inadequate: Cronbach’s alpha ranged from .358 to .432, average variance extracted from .192 to .229, and all construct-pair HTMT ratios exceeded .90. The positive coefficients consequently describe associations among labelled observed scores and cannot establish distinct appraisal mechanisms. The contribution is an assessment of the mismatch between the proposed construct structure and the available indicators, together with a transparent comparison of additive and interactive specifications. Future studies should validate differentiated measures and examine observed protective behaviour before deriving intervention recommendations.

paper_title: Esophageal Injury During Transesophageal Echocardiography-Guided Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) remains an established imaging modality for guiding percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), providing real-time visualization during transseptal puncture, device deployment and procedural assessment. However, esophageal instrumentation and prolonged probe manipulation may result in gastrointestinal injury, particularly in patients with pre-existing esophageal abnormalities or increased bleeding risk. This narrative review summarizes the available evidence regarding the mechanisms, risk factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, management and prevention of TEE-associated esophageal injury during LAAO while examining alternative imaging strategies. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by targeted searches of broader structural heart intervention literature. Although clinically recognized TEE-associated gastrointestinal complications are uncommon, studies employing systematic endoscopic surveillance have identified substantially higher rates of subclinical mucosal injury. Reported manifestations range from transient dysphagia and superficial mucosal lesions to gastrointestinal bleeding, intramural esophageal hematoma, perforation and fistula formation. Nevertheless, limited LAAO-specific evidence, heterogeneous outcome definitions and differences in surveillance strategies preclude reliable estimation of procedure-specific esophageal injury incidence. Intracardiac echocardiography eliminates esophageal instrumentation but carries a distinct procedural risk profile, whereas cardiac computed tomography (CCT) provides complementary opportunities for preprocedural planning and postprocedural surveillance. Careful preprocedural assessment, judicious probe manipulation, early recognition of complications and individualized imaging selection are important considerations. Prospective studies incorporating standardized esophageal injury endpoints are needed to establish the true clinical burden and guide preventive strategies.

paper_title: The Role of Fuel to Oxidant Ratios in Solution Combustion Synthesis (SCS): A Short Review
paper_abstract: Solution Combustion Synthesis (SCS) continues to emerge as a green synthesis method for the preparation of advanced inorganic nanomaterials with tailored physicochemical properties. This review discusses the basic concepts of fuel–oxidizer ratios in solution combustion synthesis and explores in detail the effects of different types of fuel-oxidizer mixtures, oxidizer nature, fuel type, experimental conditions, and targeted material properties on the optimization of combustible mixtures. Furthermore, highlights on the impact of varying fuel–oxidizer ratios on powder properties and their performance in different applications such as biosensing, catalysis, photocatalysis, and electrochemical energy storage were analyzed. Findings demonstrate that careful modulation of the combustible mixture enables structured tuning of nanomaterial properties for specific technological applications. However, despite the significant progress achieved in solution combustion synthesis, challenges still exist with controlling the combustion reaction, carbonaceous impurities, scalability, and morphology regulation. Hence, the review suggest that future perspectives should focus on the integration of advanced thermodynamic modelling, real-time in situ characterization techniques, and the development of novel fuels and oxidants to achieve improved combustion precision and reproducibility. These advancements are expected to enhance the scalability and industrial applicability of SCS while enabling the design of next-generation functional nanomaterials with superior performance and sustainability.

paper_title: A Review of Complexity Measures from Epiplexity to Algorithmic Information Dynamics
paper_abstract: Complexity science has proposed many measures of complexity, structure, information, emergence and (self-)organisation, often in isolation and without systematic understanding of their relationships, redundancies or distinct properties. As new measures continue to appear, comparative assessment is increasingly needed. Here, we systematically compare classical and recent complexity measures, characterising their relationships and sensitivities in discriminating the qualitative behaviour of discrete and continuous dynamical systems. The primary analysis used an initial 11-system benchmark comprising four elementary cellular automata, Lorenz dynamics, Mandelbrot and Julia fractals, three Boolean-network topologies, and a yeast association network. Across the binarization threshold sweep, Block-level Algorithmic Information Dynamics (AID) (\( |\Delta\mathrm{BDM}| \)) preserved cross-system rankings with mean Spearman agreement 0.881 (95\% CI, 0.848--0.910), \( \mathrm{ICC}(3,1)=0.893 \), and Kendall's \( W=0.894 \). Independent validation comprised a five-regime ladder spanning trivial/ordered, periodic/ordered, critical, chaotic, and maximally random dynamics, together with a continuous logistic-map sweep. In the categorical analysis, 2-D cell and block AID ranked first and second, respectively, in the task-specific composite combining categorical discrimination, Lyapunov tracking, and assigned perturbation capability. Post-hoc, 1-D BDM and Epiplexity separated critical from chaotic dynamics. Epiplexity and expiplexity-derived coding statistics did not distinguish chaotic from maximally random endpoints, whereas AID additionally retained signed, localised, multiscale intervention effects. Sequential structural epiplexity \( S_T \) separated validation categories (\( \epsilon_H^2=0.626 \), 95\% interval 0.515--0.782), with a much lower point separation effect size than Cell and Block AID (BDM perturbation). We develop a proposed characterisation of Epiplexity as a functional over an AID information landscape, making explicit the sufficiency assumptions needed to identify it with the original bounded-MDL definition. Thus, CTM/BDM provide estimators of algorithmic information, AID provides the perturbational calculus, and explicitly constructed scalar observables project selected aspects of that landscape.

paper_title: Farmers’ Knowledge and Use of New Agricultural Technologies in Greece: Evidence from a Nationwide Survey and Implications for Farmer Education and Training
paper_abstract: Smart agricultural technologies can improve input efficiency and environmental performance, but their benefits depend on farmers’ knowledge and use. This study assessed knowledge and use of new agricultural technologies among Greek crop farmers, perceptions of sustainable agriculture and environmental impacts, and the usefulness of agricultural education. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from September 2023 to May 2024 among 1,054 crop farmers across all 13 Greek regions using convenience sampling. Pearson’s chi-square tests and Cramer’s V examined associations between technology knowledge and age, education, and agricultural experience. Overall, 56.8% reported knowledge of new technologies, 29.7% reported technologically equipped machinery, and 17.9% reported using such technologies. Knowledge was significantly associated with age (χ²(4) = 64.41, V = 0.249), education (χ²(5) = 204.02, V = 0.444), and experience (χ²(9) = 182.51, V = 0.420; all p < 0.001). Furthermore, 70.1% reported no knowledge of sustainable agriculture, while the perceived usefulness of agricultural education was very high (mean = 4.73/5). The findings indicate a gap between reported technological knowledge and actual use and support practical training in smart machinery, digital skills, environmental protection, and agronomic practices. Given the cross-sectional design, convenience sampling, and self-reported measures, the observed associations should not be interpreted causally.

paper_title: Human Forensic Biobanks: A Scoping Review Protocol
paper_abstract: Human forensic biobanks preserve biological materials and associated information for forensic investigation, evidence retention, research, quality assurance, method development, and training, yet the terminology, purposes, governance, and operating models of these resources remain heterogeneous across forensic disciplines. This scoping review will map how human forensic biobanks and related forensic imaging or data repositories are defined, established, operated, governed, and used. The review will follow the Arksey and O’Malley framework with refinements by Levac and colleagues and will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Embase will be searched without date, geographic, or search-language restrictions, supplemented by reference-list and forward-citation searching. Eligible evidence will describe established human biological collections, retained biological evidence repositories, or qualifying forensic digital repositories with documented forensic purposes. Two reviewers will independently screen records; data will be charted using a piloted form and verified by a second reviewer. Findings will be synthesized descriptively and narratively, with publications distinguished from unique resources and physical, digital, and hybrid models mapped separately. The review is expected to characterize resource purposes, populations, specimens, and data types, governance, access, quality management, sustainability, and reported applications, while identifying implementation challenges and reporting gaps. By organizing a fragmented literature around the underlying resources rather than individual analytical findings, the review will provide a structured evidence base for future forensic biobank development, governance, and research.

paper_title: Methodologies for Developing Consumption-Based Urban GHG Emission Inventories: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: As cities emerge as the primary drivers of global consumption-based emissions, the need for greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting methods that model multisectoral urban interactions has become paramount. In this context, consumption-based (CB) urban GHG emission inventories have arisen as a useful tool for political decision-makers. This systematic literature review was carried out across three databases, covering al-most 20 years of publications strictly related to the elaboration of CB GHG emission inventories, reaching a total of 100 publications. More than a third of the articles ex-plored Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), 34% used Environmentally-Extended In-put-Output Analysis (EEIOA), with only 10% delving into hybrid methodologies. A case study comparison was performed for cities that applied different methodologies, in terms of carbon footprint. The strengths and weaknesses of each framework were also assessed. The results showed that both EEIOA and LCA were useful to model complex carbon flows and accounted for the majority of emissions associated to urban activity. EEIOA excelled for its operational simplicity and speed in the calculation of carbon footprint when input-output matrices are available, but it was not as suitable for policy-making. LCA required a larger volume of information and its processing was more time-consuming, but it was also capable of identifying hotspots. Hybrid approaches obtained carbon footprint results similar to those of EEIOA or LCA, while covering certain weaknesses of these standalone methodologies.

paper_title: Primary Hyperparathyroidism Beyond Calcium: FGF23 Dynamics After Parathyroidectomy and the Unresolved Postoperative PTH Phenotype—A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is definitively treated by parathyroidectomy (PTx), with surgical cure conventionally defined by sustained normocalcemia. However, some patients develop elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentrations despite normal postoperative calcium levels. This heterogeneous condition may reflect vitamin D insufficiency, reduced calcium availability, skeletal remineralization, or renal dysfunction, but may occasionally indicate persistent parathyroid autonomy or precede biochemical recurrence. Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), an osteocyte-derived regulator of phosphate excretion and calcitriol synthesis, occupies a central position within the bone–kidney–parathyroid axis and may participate in metabolic adaptation after PTx. This narrative review examines FGF23 regulation, circulating concentrations, clinical associations, and perioperative dynamics in PHPT. A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 11 original clinical studies directly evaluating FGF23 in PHPT. Findings were discordant: some studies reported increased preoperative concentrations and a postoperative decline, whereas others found normal levels or no significant change after surgery. Differences in disease phenotype, renal function, vitamin D status, assay methodology, supplementation, and sampling time may partly explain this heterogeneity. Notably, no study related perioperative FGF23 changes to subsequent PTH trajectories, and studies of postoperative eucalcemic PTH elevation did not measure FGF23. FGF23 cannot currently be considered a diagnostic or prognostic biomarker in PHPT. Nevertheless, serial assessment alongside conventional mineral-metabolism parameters may clarify endocrine adaptation after PTx and determine whether biologically distinct postoperative phenotypes exist.

paper_title: Optimizing Malaria and Communicable Disease Interventions: A Comprehensive Review of Mathematical Models to Control Malaria
paper_abstract: Malaria remains a major global public health challenge, with a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa and other tropical and subtropical regions. The complex transmission process involving Plasmodium parasites, Anopheles mosquito vectors, and human hosts makes mathematical modeling an important tool for understanding transmission dynamics and evaluating control strategies. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of mathematical modeling approaches for malaria transmission and control, including deterministic compartmental models, stochastic models, optimal control frameworks, spatial models, and cost-effectiveness analyses. Particular attention is given to major intervention strategies, including vector control, vaccination, antimalarial treatment, and other integrated control approaches. The review also examines the effects of seasonality, climate variability, drug and insecticide resistance, spatial heterogeneity, and human movement on malaria transmission and intervention outcomes. A bibliography-based keyword frequency analysis and word-cloud visualization are used to identify dominant research themes, followed by a comparative assessment of modeling approaches and intervention strategies. The findings highlight the importance of integrating multiple interventions with context-specific epidemiological and environmental conditions. Overall, mathematical models provide valuable support for optimizing malaria control strategies and addressing important challenges toward malaria elimination.

paper_title: Social Relationships, Depressive Symptoms, and Self-Rated Health Among Adults Living Alone in South Korea: An Analysis of the 2025 Korea Community Health Survey
paper_abstract: This study examined associations between social relationships, depressive symptoms, and self-rated health (SRH) among adults living alone in South Korea. Data from 44,168 adults living alone who participated in the 2025 Korea Community Health Survey were analyzed using complex-samples logistic regression. Social relationships included contact frequency with family members or relatives, neighbors, and friends and neighborhood trust. Depressive symptoms were defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score ≥ 10. The weighted prevalence of depressive symptoms was 6.9%, and that of poor SRH was 22.5%. Compared with contact four or more times per week, family or relative contact less than once per month was associated with depressive symptoms (aOR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.31–1.72) and poor SRH (aOR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.17–1.41). Corresponding associations for infrequent friend contact were stronger (aOR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.75–2.34; aOR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.63–1.93, respectively). Lack of neighborhood trust was also associated with both outcomes. These findings suggest that specific social relationships, particularly friendships, are relevant to mental and perceived health among adults living alone.

paper_title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
paper_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly improving on long-horizon scientific and olympiad tasks. Recent systems have produced a Lean-formalized resolution of the Navier--Stokes problem and autonomous solutions to four open questions in the Erdős Conjectures database. Yet neither system releases both its underlying model and complete inference stack. More broadly, a single agent session remains brittle on difficult problems: early errors can propagate, missing domain knowledge can stall progress, and apparent success can mask a misinterpretation or weakening of the original task. We introduce HOA (Humanize Olympiads Agent), an open, flow-level framework that coordinates multiple agent sessions through three complementary feedback channels. First, an independent reviewer evaluates each candidate and provides actionable feedback. Second, a structured wiki supplies task-specific knowledge that may be missing or unreliable in model pretraining. Third, a verifier checks generated Lean proofs against trusted challenge statements. With GPT-5.6 Sol, HOA achieves perfect scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI 2026, near-full marks on the IChO 2026 problem set, and solves all 672 problems (100%) on PutnamBench. On the Lean-Eval leaderboard, HOA ranks first, solving 251 of 304 problems (82.6%). We further evaluate HOA with open models. Using Kimi-K3, HOA achieves full scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI, and a gold-level score of 97.1% on the IChO. These results closely match the closed-source GPT-5.6 Sol + /Goal baseline on the IMO and IPhO, while exceeding it on the IChO and IOI, demonstrating that systematic feedback can help bridge substantial differences in base-model capability.

paper_title: From Cell Chemistry to Combat Power: A Mission-Driven Review of Battery-Dependent and Electrically Powered Military Systems
paper_abstract: Military capability increasingly depends on electrical energy for sensing, communications, computing, autonomy, mobility, protection, electronic warfare, and electrically enabled weapons. However, the value of a battery or energy-storage technology cannot be judged from chemistry or cell-level energy density alone. This review develops a mission-driven framework linking cell chemistry → module/pack → power electronics and thermal management → platform integration → mission effect → operational energy and contested logistics. It distinguishes energy from power and organizes military systems into four analytical battery roles: battery-integral, battery-dependent, battery-buffered, and battery-secondary. The framework is applied across soldier systems, smart munitions, unmanned systems, tactical vehicles, naval platforms, and high-power electrically enabled systems. The review finds that no universal “best military battery” exists; technology selection must reflect mission duty cycle, power demand, environmental exposure, survivability, recharge or resupply conditions, and system integration. Cell-level advantages can be reduced by pack overhead, protection, thermal management, power conversion, degradation, maintainability, and logistics. The review also proposes a cross-level evidence framework that distinguishes cell, pack, platform, modeled, demonstrated, operational, and fielded evidence. These findings support a mission-driven transition roadmap and strategic implications for force design, acquisition, research priorities, and operational-energy planning.

paper_title: Vesicular Protocells at the Origin of Life: A Critical Review and a Bounded Bio-Inspired Analogy
paper_abstract: Membrane-bounded vesicles assembled from prebiotically plausible amphiphiles remain one of the most experimentally supported models of early compartmentalization. Mixed single-chain amphiphiles form vesicles over a wider pH and salinity range than early single-component fatty-acid systems; such vesicles can grow, divide by physically or chemically simple routes, and, in selected formulations, host limited nonenzymatic nucleic-acid chemistry. This article reviews those results, with emphasis on work since the 2018 syntheses of Joyce and Szostak and of Chen and Walde, and separates them from a second, independent question: whether modern microbial biofilms can be used as functional analogs when thinking about matrix-stabilized compartments.The two questions are independent in claim-type and must not be fused, but they are linked by an explicit translation rule. Extracellular polymeric substances, short-chain fatty acids, and other products of evolved metabolism are not demonstrated prebiotic building blocks. A publicly posted preprint by the present author coupled a vesicular framework to microbial-biofilm language [20]. Preliminary morphological observations of heat-treated probiotic biofilms after rehydration, developed in drafts leading to that preprint, do not establish a vesicle-to-cell transition, do not document sterility, and cannot be read as abiogenesis. Even a later, well-controlled demonstration of survival after autoclaving would concern persistence of pre-existing biological material, not the emergence of cells from nonliving chemistry. An informal coupling of pH gradients to zeta potential is retained only as a qualitative analogy that currently lacks defined variables, energy accounting, kinetics, and falsifying predictions.The recommended path is therefore split in its inferences and joined in its constraints: a microbiological study of matrix-protected survival, if pursued at all, should meet sterilization-validation standards and remain silent on origin-of-life claims; protocell experiments should start from abiotic amphiphile mixtures and specified geochemical boundary conditions, and should obey the same translation rules used to reject the biofilm reading. Within those limits, vesicular models continue to offer a coherent experimental program for the chemistry-to-biology transition.

paper_title: Urban Region Representation Learning: A Survey of Data, Methodological Families, Applications, and Evaluation
paper_abstract: Urban computing increasingly relies on representations of bounded areas such as neighborhoods, census tracts, and traffic-analysis zones. Urban Region Representation Learning (URRL) transforms heterogeneous spatial-structural data, human mobility, POIs and urban text, urban imagery, and societal or environmental evidence into reusable region representations for functional inference, socioeconomic estimation, mobility and demand prediction, and emerging urban reasoning tasks. The URRL literature spans statistical context and spatial-smoothness modeling, graph-based relational learning, contrastive and self-supervised alignment, and foundation-model-based knowledge transfer and task adaptation. Although existing surveys provide valuable perspectives on urban data fusion and broad geospatial representation learning, they do not jointly examine the region as the learned unit, the hybrid composition of modern URRL systems, and the comparability of their evaluation protocols. To address this gap, we review URRL through an integrated data-method-application-evaluation framework. We examine how urban evidence is aggregated to regions and constrained by scale, vintage, coverage, and measurement bias. We then organize representative methods into four dominant, non-exclusive families and use inductive bias to interpret their representation mechanisms, learning signals, and imported knowledge. Finally, we synthesize applications and develop a protocol-aware evaluation framework that distinguishes resources, experimental configurations, and public benchmarks, while separating within-city reuse from geographic, partition, temporal, and missing-evidence generalization.

paper_title: Prismatic Image Relocation in Macular Disease: Effects on Visual Function and the Preferred Retinal Locus-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of prismatic image relocation for visual rehabilitation in patients with macular disease and central vision loss, focusing on visual acuity, reading-related outcomes, preferred retinal locus (PRL) behaviour, fixation, and functional outcomes. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261500738). Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed/MEDLINE, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to September 2026. Randomized, non-randomized comparative, pre-post, and case-series studies evaluating prism-based image relocation were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, or the appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed when studies were sufficiently comparable. Results: Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria. Two randomized controlled trials provided comparable data for the primary meta-analysis of distance visual acuity. The pooled point estimate was in the direction of better visual acuity with prism correction but was imprecise and included the null effect (MD, −0.218 logMAR; 95% CI, −0.522 to 0.086), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 94.5%). The certainty of evidence for the primary outcome was rated as very low. Sensitivity analyses did not materially strengthen the evidence. Observational studies frequently reported favourable visual or functional outcomes, but several were affected by important risks of selection bias, confounding, or absence of appropriate control groups. Conclusions: The available evidence indicates that prismatic image relocation can modify retinal image position and may provide visual or functional benefit in selected patients with central vision loss, although the certainty of evidence regarding its effect on distance visual acuity is very low.

paper_title: Genetic Engineering and Evolution Across Biological Systems: A Structured Review of the Origin, Transmission, and Population Fate of Engineered Variation
paper_abstract: Genetic engineering deliberately alters biological material, but the transmission, spread, and continued function of engineered variation remain subject to evolutionary processes. This structured narrative review compares engineered crops, insect gene drives, and engineered microbes through an origin–transmission–population fate framework, distinguishing control at the sequence, inheritance, and ecological levels. Crop studies document pollen-mediated gene flow, multi-year transgene persistence in a weedy relative, and pest resistance alongside regional pest suppression. Gene-drive studies demonstrate biased inheritance and collapse of particular cage populations, while resistance and ecological heterogeneity constrain extrapolation to other settings. Microbial studies show that construct burden, genetic exchange, and selection can undermine intended functions despite successful initial engineering and host colonization. Together, these findings distinguish molecular precision from control over inheritance, population persistence, and ecological outcomes: initial technical success does not establish lasting practical benefit. The review maps research designs to the claims they can support and identifies difficulties in comparison across systems, interpretation of evidence, and observation over relevant evolutionary time scales. Priorities include multigenerational monitoring, comparable measures of genetic persistence and functional stability, and staged, context-sensitive evaluation. The framework connects molecular intervention with population processes and clarifies the evidence needed for biosafety and governance decisions.

paper_title: A Design-Based Mood’s Median Test for Complex Survey Data
paper_abstract: Comparing central tendency across groups in complex survey data is challenging when outcome variables are skewed or contain outliers. While Mood’s median test provides a robust nonparametric solution under simple random sampling, it is not directly applicable to data arising from complex survey designs. This article proposes a design-based extension that integrates weighted median estimation with Rao–Scott adjusted tests of independence.The method replaces sample counts with estimated population totals derived from survey weights and uses design-consistent variance estimation to account for clustering, stratification, and unequal probabilities of selection. A Rao–Scott correction is then applied to obtain valid inference. The approach is demonstrated using data from a WHO STEPS survey, highlighting its practical utility in epidemiological applications.

paper_title: Geographic Variations in the Clinical and Hematological Manifestations of Pediatric Visceral Leishmaniasis: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Background: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL), or kala-azar, is one of the most devastating neglected tropical diseases, disproportionately affecting children in resource-limited endemic regions across four major geographic zones. Despite decades of research, no comprehensive systematic review has rigorously compared clinical and hematological manifestations of pediatric VL across these regions, leaving clinicians without evidence-based, region-specific guidelines. Objectives: To analyze and compare the clinical, hematological, and epidemiological patterns of pediatric VL across four major endemic regions: Mediterranean/Europe, Latin America, East/Central Africa, and Asia (West, Central, and East). Secondary objectives included comparing parasite species distributions, diagnostic approaches, treatment regimens, complication profiles, and case-fatality rates. Methods: A systematic literature search following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and PRISMA-S reporting standards was conducted across Pub-Med/MEDLINE, Scopus, ISI Web of Science, EMBASE, and CINAHL. The review protocol was retrospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; Registration No.: CRD420261446750). Retrospective PROSPERO registration is acknowledged as a limitation of this review. Duplicate records were removed using Rayyan software. From 1,482 identified records, after removing 117 duplicates and applying pre-specified inclusion/exclusion criteria, 40 studies met all eligibility criteria: Mediterranean/Europe (n=13), Latin America (n=6), East/Central Africa (n=6), and Asia (n=15). Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. Cross-tabulations were performed for exploratory descriptive purposes; results are presented as narative synthesis. Results: Apparent geographic variations were observed. Fever was near-universal (91-100%) across all regions. Splenomegaly ranged from 90% to 98%, and hepatomegaly from 65% to 89%. Anemia prevalence ranged from 78% to 95%, pancytopenia from 45% to 72%, and thrombocytopenia from 62% to 92% (based on exploratory cross-tabulations). Leishmania infantum predominated in Mediterranean/European and Latin American regions; L. donovani prevailed in African and Asian cohorts. Treatment regimens, diagnostic methods, and complication profiles showed substantial regional differences. Conclusions: Apparent geographic variations exist in pediatric VL manifestations, which may be associated with differences in parasite species, host genetics, nutritional status, healthcare infrastructure, and co-infection patterns. Region-specific diagnostic and therapeutic guidelines are urgently needed and should be supported by enhanced surveillance and collaborative international research.

paper_title: Clinical Applications of Metabolomics in Paediatric Brain Tumours and Other Solid Tumours: A Review
paper_abstract: There is growing interest in utilising metabolomics as a tool in childhood cancer research. We propose four main applications of metabolomics in this context; as a less invasive diagnostic technique, to identify prognostic biomarkers, to monitor disease progression or detect relapse and to identify novel therapeutic targets. MEDLINE, PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane databases were searched. Studies evaluating metabolomics in paediatric brain and other solid tumours in the context of our four applications were included. Studies evaluating other ‘omics’ modalities, tumour types, outcomes or involving adults were excluded. 39 articles were included. Published evidence in brain tumours includes the potential for metabolomics to identify biomarkers from peripheral blood samples, possibly obviating the need for invasive biopsies. Additionally, magnetic resonance spectroscopy adds value to conventional magnetic resonance imaging for diagnosis and prognostication. Considering other solid tumours, metabolomics has been evaluated in neuroblastoma for risk stratification of disease and in osteosarcoma, retinoblastoma, Wilms tumour and hepatoblastoma for identifying novel diagnostic biomarkers and improving understanding of tumour pathophysiology. Our review highlights the wide-ranging applications of metabolomics across paediatric brain and other solid tumours. There is an emerging role for metabolomics within research and clinical spheres to improve the diagnosis and management of childhood cancers.

paper_title: Review of Power Management Integrated Circuits for Energy Harvesting
paper_abstract: This manuscript presents a review of Power Management Integrated Circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting applications, covering both commercial off-the-shelf components and academic custom designs reported between 2014 and mid-2026. A two-round search across seven databases processed 1393 sources, of which 102 met the inclusion criteria after deduplication and screening. The review addresses the principal harvesting modalities considered in the literature surveyed, that is, solar/photovoltaic, thermoelectric, piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid/multisource systems, and examines commercial PMICs alongside state-of-the-art academic prototypes, including designs reported at ISSCC 2025 and ISSCC 2026 conferences. Real-world deployment cases with measured results are analyzed across five application domains: IoT sensor nodes, wearable and implantable devices, structural health monitoring, UAV energy harvesting, and unconventional sources. Key performance metrics are compared, including quiescent current, cold-start voltage, minimum operating voltage, conversion efficiency, and MPPT performance. Academic designs have demonstrated quiescent currents as low as 32 nA, cold-start operation at 57 mV, sustained converter operation from 3.5 mV after startup, and MPPT efficiencies exceeding 99%. Controlled comparisons of commercial PMICs show that their relative performance depends strongly on source impedance, voltage level, excitation conditions, and startup requirements; accordingly, a first-pass selection procedure organized by operating regime is proposed. Five trends shaping next-generation PMICs are identified: inductorless charge-pump architectures, batteryless intermittent-computing integration, TinyML on harvested energy, multi-source chip-level integration, and advanced CMOS integration, represented in the surveyed literature by implementations down to 28 nm FDSOI.
